text.p: Airport Systems International Inc said Tuesday it is evaluating strategic alternatives to enhance shareholder value.
Among the alternatives being explored are joint ventures, mergers, acquisitions and strategic alliances, it added.

"The board of directors of Airport Systems has directed the officers of the company to explore financial and business strategies with a view toward maximizing shareholder value," Keith Cowan, president, said in a statement.
Airport Systems also said it retained Goldsmith, Agio, Helms and Co, a Minneapolis-based investment banking firm, to assist with the evaluation.
The company said its backlog as of April 30 stood at $20 million, up from $6.5 million a year ago. It projects revenue of approximately $20 million versus $14.2 million in fiscal 1996.

"Based on our current schedules, we continue to expect a favorable year-to-year comparison in net income in the fourth quarter and believe that results for fiscal 1997 as a whole will include a solid profit for our shareholders," Cowan said. "In addition, we expect improvement in our results for fiscal 1998."
Airport Systems designs, manufactures, markets and installs ground-based equipment and airfield signs to aid the in-flight navigation and ground movement of aircraft.
